## Description

Validates that `tabBarPlacement` set to `bottom` keeps the tab bar at the bottom of the screen in a regular horizontal size class, where iPadOS moves it to the top by default, and that `automatic` restores the default. Guards against the tab bar going back to the top on iPad, on rotation or while resizing the window.

## Note

The prop is supported on iOS 18 and later. Below it, `bottom` only logs a warning and the tab bar keeps the default placement.

## Steps - iPad

### Baseline

1. Launch the app and navigate to the **Tab Bar Placement** screen.

    - [ ] The tab bar is displayed at the top with Tab1 and Tab2.
    - [ ] The picker shows `automatic`.

2. Set tabBarPlacement = `bottom`.

    - [ ] The tab bar moves to the bottom of the screen.

---

### Layout

1. Rotate the device to landscape.

    - [ ] The tab bar stays at the bottom.

2. Rotate back to portrait, shrink the app window to an iPhone-like width with
   the resize handle, then make it full size again.

    - [ ] The tab bar stays at the bottom in both sizes.

3. Switch to Tab2 and scroll to the end of the list.

    - [ ] The last row is visible above the tab bar.

---

### Restore

1. Go back to Tab1 and set tabBarPlacement = `automatic`.

    - [ ] The tab bar moves back to the top.

## Steps - iPhone

### Baseline

1. Launch the app and navigate to the **Tab Bar Placement** screen.

    - [ ] The tab bar is displayed at the bottom.

2. Switch tabBarPlacement between `automatic` and `bottom`.

    - [ ] The tab bar stays at the bottom with both values.
